Real data: k\*, z, Q for **all** M(M-1)/2 pairs per dataset (Arena 2016; judges 2016 each; MT-Bench 15; NBA season <= 435), both families.

- Scaling: log k\* = a + b log z + c log N + d log P: b = 1.11 (delete) / 1.13 (flip), c = 0.45 / 0.43 (theory 1 and 0.5), residual sd 0.23 / 0.20 (log).
- Q = k\* gmax / gap under correctly specified BT: delete mean log Q = -0.03 (Q ~ 0.97; 0.90 sparse-no-ties .. 1.06 dense-ties), instance-level sd of mean log Q = 0.06 within a
  configuration; flip: mean log Q = +0.21, depends on density (sparse 1.08-1.10, dense 1.28-1.35 because the capacity of the top-influence alterations is used up). So **Q is not >= 1** under exact refit
  (the brief's inequality holds for the linear regime only) and its baseline depends on graph and family: Q is only read against its own null (same graph).
- First-order search: k_lin / k_ver median 1.26 (delete; first-order overestimates because influence grows as data is removed), 0.97 (flip).
- **Positive control (`scripts/14_positive_control.py`).** Synthetic data (all rows `synthetic=1`) simulated from the fitted BT of two real graphs: Arena-55k (M = 64, 1,275 pairs, same pair counts and tie rate, N = 57,477;

  Each simulated data set goes through the same rule as the real data: BT fit on pair-aggregated counts, own same-graph null (8 replicates, 300 pairs), Delta(log Q) = mean over pairs with z_fisher in [1,8] of log Q - log Q_null, jackknife interval over models, margin 0.15, delete and flip.
  Pairs are a z-spread sample of the 300 pairs in z_fisher in [0.7, 10] (Arena) or all (M = 6). Replicates: 5 per condition on Arena-55k, 20 on MT-Bench human (null: 8 replicates on Arena-55k, 20 on the 6-model graph, which has only 15 pairs). Reported per condition: Delta, interval, share of replicates whose interval lies inside / beyond +-0.15 (detected = beyond, or the pooled mean beyond),
  and the smallest departure size whose pooled interval leaves +-0.15 (reported as "not reached" if none does). "Q is insensitive to this departure" is the reported outcome where no size is detected. SE ratios of the same simulated data sets are recorded (cluster and comparison bootstrap, B = 200). Before this revision a smoke test of the code (one replicate of Arena-55k `overdisp` 0.5 with 2 null replicates and 60 pairs, two replicates of MT-Bench human `overdisp` 1.0) had been run t

shown.message:
I've pushed `results/positive_control.csv` to my repo's `main` and to `paper-repo` `dev` (dd36f6d). It's partial: MT-Bench human is complete, but only four Arena-55k cells exist so far.

- **MT-Bench human:** every departure and size, plus the no-departure control, for delete and flip.
- **Arena-55k:** the cells finished so far are the no-departure control, overdispersion 0.25, position 0.25 and pair-specific deviation 0.1.
- **Replicates:** on MT-Bench, 1–6 of the 20 replicates per cell drop out, because they have fewer than 5 pairs with z_fisher in [1,8]. `n_replicates` is the number used and `replicates_run` the number run.
- **Sizes:** I recorded the reason for them in `REPRODUCE.md`. They were fixed in advance on the logit scale, from small up to large enough to find where the test breaks. They are not calibrated to departures measured in real data, so "not detected" applies only to those sizes.

I replied on `experiment-repo`#10 to the `paper-repo` request, and noted the delivery on #9. #7, #9 and #10 stay open until the Arena cells arrive.

I'm ending this turn. The Arena jobs wake me when they finish, and then I'll rerun `scripts/15_control_table.py`, deliver the full table and close the three issues.
